## 2B.7 Research Note: Kishida in 2024

Overall reading: **mostly yes**. Kishida repeatedly backed ceasefire-adjacent diplomacy, UN/charter-based settlements, and post-conflict humanitarian steps on Ukraine and Gaza. The main limitation is that he often did this while also backing deterrence-heavy security policy, so the record is pro-settlement more than pure peacemaking.

### Supports
- **[Summit on Peace in Ukraine (Summary)](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202406/15ukraine.html)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 15, 2024 | Kishida called for a “just and lasting peace” grounded in the UN Charter and international law, and rejected unilateral changes by force or coercion. He also said Japan would contribute to nuclear safety, electricity, and mine action, which is consistent with post-conflict recovery and reconciliation. | `2B.7`, `2B.4`, `2B.1`

- **[Signing of the Accord on Support for Ukraine and Cooperation between the Government of Japan and Ukraine (Summary)](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202406/13accord.html)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | June 13, 2024 | The accord covered humanitarian support, recovery/reconstruction, and cooperation under Japan’s constitutional and legal requirements. That is a lawful settlement / post-conflict reconstruction posture rather than open-ended militarization. | `2B.7`, `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.7`

- **[G7 Leaders’ statement on Gaza](https://www.mofa.go.jp/ecm/ec/pageite_000001_00384.html)** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | June 4, 2024 | Japan joined a statement calling for hostage release, humanitarian aid, protection of civilians, compliance with international humanitarian law, and de-escalation. This is strong ceasefire-adjacent evidence. | `2B.7`, `2B.4`, `2B.1`

- **[On the Current Situation Surrounding the Gaza Strip](https://www.mofa.go.jp/press/release/pressite_000001_00630.html)** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | October 7, 2024 | Japan condemned the Hamas attacks, demanded hostage release, described Gaza’s humanitarian situation as critical, and urged all parties including Israel to comply with international humanitarian law and work toward ceasefire. This is direct support for a lawful, diplomatic settlement track. | `2B.7`, `2B.4`, `2B.1`

- **[G7 Leaders’ Video Conference](https://www.mofa.go.jp/ecm/ec/pageit_000001_00279.html)** | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan | April 15, 2024 | Kishida said Iran’s attack on Israel would further deteriorate the situation and stressed self-restraint to prevent escalation. He also said Japan would help protect and evacuate citizens. That is a clear de-escalation / confidence-building move. | `2B.7`, `2B.4`, `2B.1`, `1B.8`

- **[Why is Japan seeking a summit with nuclear-armed North Korea?](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/explainerwhy-is-japan-seeking-a-summit-with-nucleararmed-north-korea-3374282)** | Reuters | April 11, 2024 | Reuters reported Kishida sought face-to-face talks with Kim Jong Un, making diplomacy with a hostile nuclear-armed adversary a stated objective rather than threats or escalation. This is the clearest evidence of trying to preserve a peace channel when possible. | `2B.7`, `2B.1`, `1B.8`, `1B.6`

- **[The Ninth Japan-China-ROK Trilateral Summit (Summary)](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/diplomatic/202405/27chnrok.html)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | May 27, 2024 | Kishida urged North Korea to abandon its nuclear and ballistic missile programs in line with UN Security Council resolutions. This is lawful, multilateral conflict management rather than force-first signaling. | `2B.7`, `2B.1`, `1B.6`, `1B.8`

### Limits
- **[Address by Prime Minister at a Joint Meeting of the United States Congress](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202404/11speech.html)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | April 11, 2024 | Kishida emphasized counterstrike capability, defense spending, cybersecurity, and stronger U.S. extended deterrence. This does not negate the peace-track evidence, but it shows he did not rely on diplomacy alone. | `2B.7`, `1B.4`, `1B.8`

- **[Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida regarding His Attendance at the NATO Summit and Other Matters](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/11kaiken.html)** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 11, 2024 | Kishida linked Euro-Atlantic and Indo-Pacific security and expanded Japan-NATO cooperation on cyber, space, information-sharing, and support for Ukraine. That is compatible with peacekeeping by deterrence, but it is also a harder bloc-security posture. | `2B.7`, `1B.4`, `1B.8`, `1B.9`

### Gap
- I found **no direct 2024 evidence** that Kishida personally negotiated a ceasefire in a live conflict or signed a comprehensive peace settlement.
- The record is instead **diplomatic, humanitarian, and confidence-building**, especially on Ukraine, Gaza, North Korea, and crisis de-escalation.
- Best reading: **yes, he pursued credible peace-oriented alternatives when available, but through multilateral and humanitarian channels rather than direct mediator-to-warrior bargaining.**
